title: The endocrine system

match.reason: The bank point covers glands, hormones, and receptors at a senior Biology depth, but it does not compare hormonal and nerve messaging for speed and duration, which is the idea this Year 9 Responding to stimuli point teaches.

draft.title: The endocrine system
card: The endocrine system is made up of glands. Glands release chemical messengers called hormones.
Hormones travel in the blood. They reach cells all around the body, but they only affect cells that can respond to them.
Hormone messages are slower than nerve messages, because blood carries them. Their effects often last longer, from minutes to hours or more.
Adrenaline is a hormone released by the adrenal glands in a fright. It raises heart rate and gets the body ready for action, and the effects last for a while after the danger has passed.
draft.remember: Hormones are slower than nerves, but their effects last longer.

a.q: How do hormones travel from a gland to the cells they affect?
opts: Through the air in the lungs
a.why: Glands release hormones into the blood, and the blood carries them around the body. Neurons carry nerve impulses, not hormones. Mixing these up is common, but the card says hormones use the blood.
a.clue: Think about what the body uses to carry things around.

b.q: Tom is startled by a snake on a bush track. His heart still pounds a few minutes after it slithers away. What best explains this?
opts: Hormones act faster than nerve messages
The adrenal glands have stopped working
b.why: Adrenaline is a hormone, and hormone effects last longer than nerve messages. That is why his heart keeps pounding after the danger is gone. Hormones are slower than nerves, not faster, so the second option is wrong.
b.clue: Compare how long hormone effects last with nerve effects.

problems.detail: Why (b) calls 'Hormones act faster than nerve messages' the 'second option', but the options are shown in random order, so a student may look at the wrong option. Name the option by its words instead.
The card says hormone effects 'often' last longer, but the remember line drops 'often' and states it as a general rule. Consider 'their effects often last longer'.
